q: What is AiDealDeck?

q: What is a card?
a: One tool for one part of your business: your numbers, your listings, your new leads, your money or your assistant. Each card comes with a blank workbook, a sample workbook, a START HERE guide, the setup prompt and a Setup Pack that Claude reads.

q: What does the Real Estate KPI Tracker do?
a: It tracks lead to appointment set, held, signed, under contract and closed, with the real percentage at each step. It works out the weekly number you need for the goal you type in, and shows which lead sources produce closings. More about this card.

q: What does the Listing Exposure Playbook do?
a: It gives every listing the same 14-day launch plan, with fill-in templates and day-7 and day-14 seller reports. More about this card.

q: What does the Lead-for-Life System do?
a: It lays out a follow-up plan for every new lead until they book, keeps a daily call list, scores how fast leads get a first contact, and includes a TCPA checklist. More about this card.

q: What does the Commission & GCI Ledger do?
a: It records every closing with its commission, fees, referral fees and splits, and keeps team totals separate from your own income. It is a tracking tool, not accounting software. More about this card.

q: What does the VA Playbook & Scorecard do?
a: It gives your assistant a narrow role with three jobs, a daily routine, an end-of-day report and a weekly scorecard. More about this card.

q: What is the Listing Watchdog?
a: A bonus card. You tell it which people to watch: past clients, people who went quiet after an appointment, referrals. It tells you when one of them lists with another agent, or when that listing expires or comes back. Public listing sites can be late or wrong, so always confirm on your MLS.

q: Can I use the Listing Watchdog to win back a seller who listed with someone else?
a: No. Do not contact a seller while they are listed with another agent. That can break your MLS and association rules. The Watchdog is for learning. It shows who went quiet and who you lost, so you can fix that step in your sales process and lose fewer listings. If a listing ends and the seller is free again, follow your own rules for expired listings. Always check your own rules first.
